flashcard_questions.q: What did Puritans want to remove from the Church of England?
What is Presbyterianism in Puritan thinking?
flashcard_questions.a: A church structure governed by elders rather than bishops.
The monarch’s exclusive right to decide certain matters, including religion.

flashcard_questions.q: Why was the Puritan challenge political as well as religious?
flashcard_questions.a: It questioned Elizabeth’s authority as Supreme Governor of the Church.

flashcard_questions.q: In ____, the MP Walter Strickland proposed a new prayer book to Parliament.
How did Elizabeth stop Strickland’s proposal?
flashcard_questions.a: She shut down the debate before Parliament could discuss it.

flashcard_questions.q: What were “prophesyings” in the Elizabethan Church?
flashcard_questions.a: Meetings where clergy discussed the Bible and practised preaching.

flashcard_questions.q: Which illegal pamphlets of 1588–1589 attacked bishops with satire?
Who was the pamphleteer John Stubbs?
flashcard_questions.a: A writer who attacked Elizabeth’s proposed French marriage.

flashcard_questions.q: What punishment did Elizabeth give John Stubbs?
flashcard_questions.a: His right hand was chopped off.

flashcard_questions.q: Which controversy of the 1560s saw clergy refuse the prescribed robes?
Which spymaster in Elizabeth’s government sympathised with the Puritans?
Why did organised Puritan opposition fade after 1590?
flashcard_questions.a: Leading Puritans died off and were replaced by moderates.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do some historians see the Puritans as a limited threat?
flashcard_questions.a: They never plotted to overthrow Elizabeth.

notes: 14 cards: 4 term-to-definition, 4 person-to-significance, 3 cause-effect, 3 event/date (1 cloze on 1571). Lesson has only one glossary term, so most cards are drawn from the body text.
